title: Redwood discovery with Centauri Capital - cost/unit economics
summary: Discovery focused on unit economics for LLM inference. Customer wants to understand per-token pricing, how batching and KV/prefix caching will lower costs, differences between Hosted/Dedicated/Private pricing and predictable spend, and an ask to run a short pilot/benchmark against their workload within their $25k/month budget target.
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing calculator and SKU examples
SE to propose benchmark plan and requirements
Customer to share sample prompts and token distribution
Schedule technical deep dive next week
action_items: Maya Chen - Send pricing calculator and hosted vs dedicated cost breakdown - 2026-07-23
Ravi Kapoor - Draft benchmark plan + required sample workload and infra notes - 2026-07-24
Alex Rivera - Share 2 weeks of anonymized queries and token histograms - 2026-07-25
Ben Cole - Confirm monthly budget target and procurement timeline - 2026-07-28
header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Alex Rivera (CTO - Centauri), Priya Nair (Head of ML), Ben Cole (Finance Lead), Sofia Park (Infra)
Recording ID: ff-2026-07-21-centauri-0007
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm maya, ae at redwood, and ravi is our systems eng, lena is csm. could you do quick intros?
[00:12] Alex Rivera: yeah alex here, cto at centauri. we're evaluating options for serving our inference models, mainly for document summarization and internal search. budget is tight so we're really focused on per-token costs.
[00:28] Priya Nair: hi i'm priya, head of ml. curious about batching, kv cache, and whether we should go hosted or dedicated. we also have some compliance asks.
[00:40] Ben Cole: ben from finance, i'll be tracking budget. we're targeting around $25k/month for inference spend to start.
[00:50] Ravi Kapoor: great, thanks. to frame this, can you describe your traffic profile? qps, sequence lengths, percent streaming, and peak windows?
[01:05] Sofia Park: most requests are short to medium, avg tokens per request is ~350 tokens, p95 is around 1,200, peaks during market open windows for us are 250 qps for like 10 mins.
[01:22] Priya: token distribution we've attached a histogram in the followup, but heavy tail is real. also we do a lot of repeated prefixes for templates (so caching could matter).
[01:34] Maya: perfect, that's helpful. Ben when you say $25k/mo is that all-in for hosted API, or do you expect reserved capacity?
[01:44] Ben: ideally hosted if it's within budget, otherwise we can consider a reserved/dedicated commitment if it gives predictable unit economics.
[01:52] Ravi: ok. high level differences — hosted has simple per-token pricing and no infra ops; dedicated gives reserved GPU pools, lower per-token cost at scale, predictable throughput and cost when you commit. private adds more for control/compliance.
[02:10] Alex: can you give a ballpark per-token delta? like 2x cheaper on dedicated?
[02:18] Maya: ballpark varies by model. for typical Llama-like open models on hosted you might see $0.0009 per input token / $0.0018 per output token for a certain family; with dedicated that can drop 30-60% depending on utilization and batching. numbers are illustrative, we have a calculator we'll send.
[02:36] Priya: and how much does batching help? our workload has many concurrent short requests during peaks so i'm hoping batching will shave costs without destroying latency.
[02:46] Ravi: batching is workload-dependent. if you can tolerate small additional latency on the tail, batching combined with continuous batching in our runtime can increase GPU efficiency a lot. for many profiles we've seen effective per-token cost reductions of 20-40% purely from batching at similar quality/throughput. also prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts can drop generation compute substantially — sometimes 50% less tokens computed if you're able to cache prefixes server-side.
[03:12] Ben: is cache automatic on hosted? any retention TTLs?
[03:18] Maya: hosted supports automatic prefix and kv caching by default with conservative defaults (short TTLs), you can tune retention on dedicated/private. for private you control KMS and cache retention policies.
[03:30] Alex: ok, what about quantization — does that impact cost/unit as well?
[03:35] Ravi: yes, quantized model variants can run faster with smaller memory footprint; they'll reduce GPU RAM and increase batch size per GPU, which lowers cost per token. tradeoffs include potential small quality deltas; we recommend A/B testing. Redwood Optimize provides recommended quantization profiles by workload.
[03:55] Priya: for compliance note — we need SOC 2 + audit logs and a VPC option. do those change cost materially?
[04:03] Maya: SOC 2 and audit logs are included for enterprise plans; VPC/private deployments have a higher baseline (platform fee + support). the main cost differential is that private means you manage infra or we ship a private control plane — that can increase fixed costs but gives data residency and control.
[04:18] Ben: how quickly can we move to dedicated if hosted exceeds budget? we don't want vendor lock-in.
[04:24] Maya: you can start hosted and move to dedicated; model versioning and rollout tools make swapping easy and we support compatibility tiers. we can estimate migration effort — usually a few weeks for production parity depending on custom infra needs.
[04:38] Alex: could you walk through a sample cost calc? say 1M output tokens and 500k input tokens per day at that token mix, with our peak patterns — what would be hosted vs dedicated?
[04:52] Ravi: quick thumb: hosted with the illustrative rates earlier, daily cost = (500k * $0.0009) + (1M * $0.0018) = $450 + $1,800 = $2,250/day ~ $67.5k/month. That overshoots your $25k target. With batching and KV caching and dedicated discount — let's apply 30% batching savings and 40% dedicated discount: effective monthly ~ $67.5k * 0.7 * 0.6 = $28.35k, still slightly above target. If caching yields more (50% compute reduction) and higher utilization on dedicated, you can get under $25k. We need your real token histograms to be sure.
[05:34] Priya: that math is super helpful — so likely we start hosted for speed and then pilot dedicated with a commit if the numbers align.
[05:42] Ben: procurement wise, our timeline is 60-90 days to approve a vendor. if costs fit we can start a pilot within 2-3 weeks.
[05:50] Maya: noted. ravi, any technical blockers you want to flag for the pilot?
[05:56] Ravi: we'll need sample workload, auth keys, estimate of latency SLOs, and if you need VPC/private we'll need network topology. For dedicated pilot we typically provision a small reserved pool and run a side-by-side benchmark for 1-2 days. We'll measure tokens/sec, latency p50/p95/p99, and token cost.
[06:18] Sofia: for VPC/private our infra team will need an architecture diagram. also curious about fallback policies — if dedicated capacity is saturated can hosted handle overflow?
[06:28] Maya: yes, smart routing supports fallback to hosted or smaller models. you can set routing policies by latency/cost/region.
[06:35] Alex: any limits on batching that might hurt our p99 latency?
[06:39] Ravi: batching introduces tail latency; our runtime supports latency-aware batching where requests with tight SLOs bypass batching. so mixed workloads are supported. We would need to tune thresholds.
[06:52] Priya: about benchmarks — what model families do you support? our prototypes use LlamaX and Mistral-variants.
[06:59] Ravi: we support curated open models including LlamaX-compatible variants, Mistral, and a few optimized forks. we also do quantized kernels and per-arch tuning. we'll include the exact kernels and expected perf in the benchmark plan.
[07:14] Ben: any hidden costs — storage, egress, logging?
[07:18] Maya: storage for caching and logs is minimal; we have optional long-retention observability add-ons that are extra. egress depends on region/provider but typical hosted API includes small egress; for private you'll manage that. we'll call out these in the calc.
[07:32] Alex: ok so next steps — we share sample traces, you send pricing calc and benchmark plan, schedule tech dive.
[07:39] Maya: yes, we'll do that. anything else?
[07:42] Priya: one more — can you run a micro-benchmark on our samples that shows end-to-end cost/latency with caching on vs off? that would help justify the committed spend to finance.
[07:52] Ravi: absolutely. that lines up with our pilot template. we'll plan a 48-hour run with caching toggles and batching profiles.
[07:59] Ben: great. i'll confirm budget timeline by 7/28.
[08:04] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the items.
[08:07] [Meeting ends]
